problem: Existing Expertise Packs can cover interface design and generic QA, but they do not encode Mux-specific playback policy, signed-token handling, live-stream lifecycle, webhook synchronization, or playback telemetry decisions.
reusable_when: Implementing or reviewing Mux-backed VOD playback in a web application
Implementing Mux Live viewer states and recording continuity
Handling Mux webhook authenticity, retries, and state synchronization
Instrumenting Mux playback health and diagnosing viewer failures
not_for: Generic video presentation or visual layout without a Mux integration
Generic product design decisions already owned by product-design
General test strategy or release QA already owned by software-qa
Broadcaster ingest infrastructure unrelated to the web playback surface
existing_coverage: product-design owns screen hierarchy, interaction, responsive behavior, and accessibility; software-qa owns generic risk, test design, state exploration, and release evidence. Neither Pack owns Mux provider contracts.

proposed_guides.failure_prevented: A web page wires playback through ad hoc URLs or incomplete player inputs and loses stream type, metadata, captions, preview, recovery, or accessibility behavior.
decision_checks: Select the player package and rendering boundary that match the target framework
Pass playback ID, stream type, metadata, media assets, and purpose-specific tokens through one typed boundary
Preserve built-in player capabilities when adding custom controls or overlays
Verify the rendered player with real Mux media and reachable error states

proposed_guides.failure_prevented: Signing credentials leak to the client, token purpose or policy is mismatched, or valid viewers lose playback because token lifetime and refresh behavior are undefined.
decision_checks: Match public, signed, or DRM policy to the playback ID and requested asset
Mint purpose-bound tokens only on a protected server after application authorization
Choose expiry and refresh behavior that cover the authorized playback window
Verify denial, expiry, refresh, and signing-key isolation paths

proposed_guides.failure_prevented: The viewer page infers live availability from local player behavior, exposes stream keys, or collapses multiple recording assets into an incorrect single-recording model.
decision_checks: Keep stream keys and ingest credentials outside public client surfaces
Map Mux live states and events to explicit viewer-facing waiting, live, reconnecting, ended, and replay states
Preserve the one-live-stream-to-many-recording-assets relationship
Define authoritative recovery and reconciliation behavior for missed live events

proposed_guides.failure_prevented: Forged, duplicated, retried, delayed, or reordered Mux webhooks corrupt durable application state.
decision_checks: Verify mux-signature against the unmodified raw request body before accepting an event
Bind the endpoint signing secret and event scope to the correct Mux environment
Make event processing idempotent, replay-safe, and tolerant of delayed delivery
Persist enough event identity and state evidence to reconcile provider and application state

proposed_guides.failure_prevented: Playback failures, slow startup, and rebuffering remain invisible or are confused with product conversion outcomes.
decision_checks: Attach stable viewer, video, and session metadata without leaking sensitive values
Observe startup, failure, rebuffering, and playback-success signals at the correct scope
Separate Mux delivery health from application authorization, UI, and business metrics
Verify telemetry in successful, denied, expired-token, offline, and fatal-player paths

pass_criteria: Mux-specific implementation goals select the candidate and only the relevant Guides
Signed playback, webhook authenticity, retry safety, and live-state criteria remain explicit
Compatibility-sensitive requests open the contextual research gate
Every frozen case has exact route and quality evidence
regression_criteria: Generic video or landing-page design does not select the Mux Pack
Generic visual hierarchy remains routed to product-design
The Pack never grants repository or external write authority
No task selects more than four Mux Guides
